hypothesis: On seeded 8-20 word windows from papers/, verify_quote accepts at least 99% of verbatim and case/whitespace-reformatted quotes and at most 1% of fabricated variants (one word substituted, two adjacent words swapped, or halves spliced from two papers); fragments shorter than three words are never accepted.
limitations: Measures exact-span grounding only. Semantic support (whether the passage supports the claim) is not tested.
Fabrications are minimal synthetic perturbations of real text, not quotes written by a model.
The corpus is the repository's papers/ snapshot; results may differ on other corpora.
The oracle encodes the documented contract; agreement shows conformance to that contract, not that the contract is the right one.

metrics.description: Share of case/whitespace-reformatted windows accepted (contract says they should be).
metrics.name: reformatted_acceptance_rate

metrics.description: Substituted + swapped + spliced cases the oracle confirms are absent from the corpus.
metrics.name: fabricated_cases

metrics.description: False-accept rate over all fabricated cases.
metrics.name: fabricated_acceptance_rate

metrics.description: Perturbed cases that the oracle found verbatim in the corpus.
metrics.name: relabeled_cases

metrics.description: Cases where verify_quote disagreed with the contract oracle.
metrics.name: oracle_disagreements

metrics.description: Share of accepted verbatim quotes attributed to the paper they were sampled from.
metrics.name: source_attribution_rate

metrics.description: Median wall time of one verify_quote call.
metrics.name: median_verify_latency_ms

procedure: Load the non-recursive citation corpus from papers/ with discover_corpus_files and hash every file.
With the seed, sample 60 windows of 8-20 whitespace tokens from papers longer than 22 tokens.

For each window build: verbatim text; random case + mixed whitespace reformatting; one interior word replaced by a word from another paper; two adjacent differing words swapped; first half spliced to a window from another paper; the first two words alone.

Label each case with an independent oracle implementing the documented contract (collapsed-whitespace, lowercased substring of one file; <3 words never). Perturbed cases the oracle finds in the corpus are relabelled genuine and excluded from the fabricated set.
Call verify_quote on every case, timing each call, and store the full case table as an artifact.
question: Does verify_quote, the quote-grounding gate used by chat, the offline demo and the MCP server, accept verbatim corpus quotes and reject minimally corrupted ones?
rationale: README states that a verified quote means the text occurs in a source. Every grounded/ungrounded label shown to users depends on this gate, so its false-accept and false-reject rates should be measured rather than assumed.
title: Citation gate rejects fabricated quotes and accepts verbatim ones
